We aim to maintain an investment grade rating to enable us to use debt comprised of unsecured, primarily fixed-rate debt (including the effect of interest rate swaps) from public markets and banks.

We expect to use cash flow from operations during the remainder of 2026 and annually thereafter for the foreseeable future to fund all of these cash requirements except for debt balloon payments due upon maturity and a portion of property development costs, the fundings for which are discussed below.
During the remainder of 2026, we expect to spend $80 million to $90 million on costs for properties actively under development, most of which was contractually obligated as of September 30, 2026.
During the remainder of 2026 and beyond, we expect to continue to actively develop additional properties and also could opportunistically acquire operating properties.

We expect to fund these activities using, in part, available cash flow from operations, with the balance funded using any excess available cash and cash equivalents and borrowings under our Revolving Development Facility and Revolving Credit Facility.

Budorick, COPT Defense’s President & Chief Executive Officer, commented, “Our track record of outperformance continued in the third quarter, as FFO per share exceeded the midpoint of our guidance by $0.02.

We increased the midpoint of guidance for 2026 FFO per share, as adjusted for comparability, by $0.02 to $2.80, which is $0.05 above our initial guidance, and absorbs $0.03 of incremental dilution from our Exchangeable Notes, resulting from our 20% share price increase over the first nine months of the year.

We increased the midpoint of 2026 guidance for Same Property cash NOI growth by 25 basis points to 4.25%, capital commitment to new investments by $40 million to $375 million, and capital invested in development and acquisitions by $15 million to $240 million.
We raised our target for vacancy leasing by over 30% from 475,000 square feet to 625,000 square feet, which is over 50% higher than our initial target of 400,000 square feet.

This increased leasing target is driven in part by our decision to proactively capture space to accommodate new higher growth tenancy in Columbia Gateway and in Huntsville, which impacts our retention guidance but de-risks future lease expirations.

We expect the FY 2026 defense budget, along with the FY 2027 base budget request in which a 28% year-over-year increase is proposed, will provide a very supportive backdrop for demand in our portfolio to support priority missions, including intelligence, cybersecurity, and missile defense.”
